## Today: Make Exploration Easy To Navigate

- Organise two plots with `tabsetPanel()` and `tabPanel()`.
- Choose controls for one group, several groups, or a numeric range.
- Use shared filtering and actionable empty-selection messages.
- Test that every tab respects the same selection.

**Outcome:** a two-tab app with group and range filters. First block: tabs. Second block: controls and feedback.

## Recall: One Selection Supplies Several Outputs {.smaller}

```{r shared-filter, eval=FALSE}
selected_data <- reactive({
  filter(d_participants, modality == input$modality)
})
```

The count and both plots use `selected_data()`. Group changes affect all three outputs; bin width affects only the histogram.

**Together:** open `intro_app.R` and choose **Run App**. Locate the shared filter and one output that uses it.

<img src="gfx/tabs-example.png" alt="The working participant app with shared controls and two tabs" style="width:100%;height:340px;object-fit:contain;">

What becomes easier when each plot has its own tab? What becomes harder to compare?

Which controls and context should remain visible when the reader changes tabs?

## Keep Shared Controls Outside The Tabs {.smaller}

```{r tabs-structure, eval=FALSE}
sidebarLayout(
  sidebarPanel(
    # Shared controls and their explanation.
  ),
  mainPanel(
    textOutput("selection_note"),
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Distribution", plotOutput("rt_plot")),
      tabPanel("Individual values", plotOutput("values_plot"))
    )
  )
)
```

`tabsetPanel()` holds the tabs; each `tabPanel()` contains its visible name and contents.

**Together:** locate the controls, count, tab names and plot locations.

## Moving A Plot Does Not Change Its Connection {.smaller}

| UI location | Server supplies |
|---|---|
| plotOutput("rt_plot") inside the first tab | output$rt_plot |
| plotOutput("values_plot") inside the second tab | output$values_plot |

Keep the output names when moving them. The existing server still works.

The server's input dependencies determine which outputs change. A control's placement in one tab does not automatically restrict it to that tab.

## Discussion: What If Nothing Is Selected? {.smaller}

<img src="gfx/empty-selection.png" alt="The app showing a recovery message when no group is selected" style="width:100%;height:300px;object-fit:contain;">

**No participants match. Select a group or widen the reaction-time range.**

Does the message explain what happened and how to recover?

Unchecking both groups or choosing a range containing no observations needs useful feedback in every affected view.

## Choose Controls For The Question {.smaller}

| Task | Control |
|---|---|
| Choose one group | `selectInput()` |
| Compare one or more groups | `checkboxGroupInput()` |
| Set a bin width | `sliderInput()` with one value |
| Keep values within an interval | `sliderInput()` with two values |

A reaction-time range filters observations. Bin width changes the summary of the observations still included.

## Checkboxes Return Several Group Values {.smaller}

```{r checkbox-example, eval=FALSE}
checkboxGroupInput(
  "groups", "Output groups",
  choices = c("Spoken output" = "speech",
              "Written output" = "writing"),
  selected = c("speech", "writing")
)
```

`input$groups` can contain speech, writing, both, or no values.

Use modality %in% `input$groups` in `filter()`: %in% checks membership in the selected values. == was suitable for the earlier single-group input.

## A Range Slider Supplies Two Numbers {.smaller}

```{r range-example, eval=FALSE}
sliderInput("rt_range", "Keep participant means within (ms)",
            min = 700, max = 2400,
            value = c(700, 2400), step = 50)
```

`input$rt_range[1]` is the lower bound; `input$rt_range[2]` is the upper bound.

```{r range-filter, eval=FALSE}
filter(d_participants,
       modality %in% input$groups,
       mean_rt >= input$rt_range[1],
       mean_rt <= input$rt_range[2])
```

Both groups together contain 72 participants across the full range.

## Wait For An Input With `req()` {.smaller}

```{r require-range, eval=FALSE}
req(input$rt_range)
```

Put this before using the range in the shared reactive expression. It pauses calculation silently until the input is available.

It does not explain an empty result to a user.

Unchecking all groups needs a visible message. We will check the filtered rows, rather than silently stopping with req(`input$groups`).

## Explain An Empty Selection With `validate()` {.smaller}

Inside the shared reactive expression, after creating selected:

```{r validate-example, eval=FALSE}
validate(need(
  nrow(selected) > 0,
  "No participants match. Select a group or widen the range."
))
selected
```

`need()` tests the condition and supplies the message when it fails. `validate()` stops this calculation and passes the feedback to outputs using it.

When rows exist, selected remains the last expression and supplies the data.

## A Small Dashboard Still Needs A Clear Purpose

The assessment permits **at most three tabs** and requires **at least two interactive plots**.

Tabs should organise useful questions. They do not replace a question, explanation or meaningful control.

Shiny-reactive plots qualify as interactive plots. Plotly hover and zoom are another option we will try next week.
